The headline: the round trip RAN, and it returns bit-identical

The wish's actual heart — round-trip fidelity, unmeasured since D127 was written — is ANSWERED. Not by argument: by four full authenticated sweeps against guerrilla at served_sha bc64d869a3a82beb1b39824196f60236b2082dbc on slot blue, ssh-confirmed PRE and POST and unchanged throughout.

default -> open -> dismiss, on the SAME page instance with no reload at any point, at 9 widths (1440, 1280, 1024, 900, 800, 764, 700, 640, 500) x 3 faces. Three of the four runs report: cells 27, identical_cells 27, returns_bit_identical TRUE. The non-identical (viewport, face, field, before, after) list D161 demands is EMPTY in every run that ran. Determinism of the same build: 0 round-trip cell diffs rt2-vs-rt3 and rt2-vs-rt4, 0 matrix field diffs across all four runs, identical click counts. Nothing drifts.

Every named assertion held in all four runs: non-zero bytes (702,496 / 718,475 / 718,490 / 718,490), 54 rows, exactly 18 is_destination true, all 18 reporting visible_meets_55ch as NULL and never FALSE, provenance_bracket.matched true with mismatches empty, zero destination_evidence disagreements across all 54 rows.
Verification results — what each assignment proved or refuted
PROVEN

round-trip-live-fire: D161(i) is MET on the deployed build, 27/27, three times over. It also caught two traps nobody had named. (1) The run-level round_trip.dismiss_control is a HALF-TRUTH — it reports widths[0] only (measure.mjs:2183), so it says 'toggle re-click, the only dismissal deployed today' while all six destination widths (900-500) actually dismiss via the purpose-built sidebar-dismiss control. Quoting the scalar would understate D161(ii), the very condition it reports on. (2) A skipped round trip EXITS 0 — the skip is a returned value, not a throw, so writeRunArtifact runs and the process exits clean. A gate reading the exit code certifies a skipped round trip as a pass.

positive-control-false-green-proof: D176's strike is now EXECUTED, not asserted. Deleting the fenced 860px generator from P's fixture entirely (657 bytes, 5715 -> 5058, no second generator surviving) and injecting the LITERAL POSITIVE_CONTROL_RULE from measure.mjs:2221-2224 flips the ::after content from none to empty-string at bucket=wide/panel=1136 — on a fixture with no threshold to certify. Reproduced byte-identically on two independently created worktrees. Mechanism understood, not just observed: no real suppressor uses !important, so an unconditional !important ::after beats every one of them regardless of specificity.

p-merge-readiness: P is a mechanical rescue, not a rebuild. Both branches are the identical commit 7b8480247; git rebase origin/main exits 0 with zero conflicts; the diff is exactly 2 pure-new files (+564, 0 modifications) touching neither measure.mjs nor root.html.heex; the offline self-test passes post-rebase and the generator-deletion mutation still flips the discriminating cell. 8 of 9 criteria already met — only the merge gate is unmet.

prediction-file-proof: the format was invented AND proven falsifiable. Composite key viewport_px|inspector_state|face, per-field basis labels, a checker that RECOMPUTES and never reads a row's own verdict, banned-scalar hygiene, three exit states. All four red paths demonstrated, including catching an artefact whose verdict contradicts its own raw numbers — the exact class studio-desk-compare.mjs:216-218 copies verbatim.
REFUTED — three premises the wave entered with were wrong

C2 REFUTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. The digest framed the three 1024 position:static warnings as 'real drift or the known ~80% non-determinism, unresolved'. Both horns are wrong: it is a STALE EXPECTATION. D108 measured 'absolute' before the Tier-2 ladder (#4922 / 4074d1986, proven inside 65541e2d4..bc64d869a by merge-base and not before it) took panes [44,260] to [44], panel 720 to 980, past the 860 generator — so the inspector legitimately docks in flow, and the reading column went 378.958px (37.90ch) to 600.000px (60.00ch). The ladder commit's own message pre-registered every figure and the deployed build returns them to the digit. Identical 6-warning set in 4 of 4 runs: zero variance.

C3 REFUTED, AND THE PREMISE CORRECTED. The digest called the plain 1024/standard row 'a clean MEET by arithmetic (panel 980, no guard applies)'. With a secondary pane open and the inspector at its SERVER DEFAULT the panel is 560, not 980, and the scrim is suppressed ONLY by the b29 guard's not-user-opened clause — a guard whose sole discriminator is the attribute the user is one click away from setting. The claimed safety margin does not exist.

D96 REFUTED. D96 ruled that D76's pressure case 'needs a cross-surface navigation no affordance offers'. It does not: the collapsed-strip expand-pane button plus the nav pane-item are both real UI and both patch-level. D175's compound state was reached end to end through real affordances — Tasks doc, open-secondary-picker (99 candidates offered), expand the 44px strip, Papers, paper — with secondary_doc surviving because Scope.select/2 is push_patch. At standard/1024 the panel is 620 = 1024-44-360 EXACTLY, and the scrim PAINTS: identical 620x500 clip, mean luminance 240.493 -> 175.104 over 310,000 pixels.

d171-gate-decision REFUTED ITS OWN ASSIGNMENT'S PREMISE. The brief said 'only two soft warnings exist'. There is only ONE, and it is about inspector.position, not buckets. Zero code anywhere compares the stamp to an expected band: D171's precondition is not weakly built, it is ENTIRELY ABSENT, and R's criterion 4 is correctly met false.
Coverage — including the not-founds

NOT FOUND (each a real gap, not an omission): scripts/measurements/open-leg-repro.mjs was never opened by the round-trip verifier — it is referenced by name in a measure.mjs comment, and Decide must NOT assume it reproduces the 1440 wide-bucket no-op, which is a DIFFERENT failure from D178's rename case. git ls-files grep predict returns nothing: no committed prediction file has ever existed in this repo, so the format had no precedent to copy. grep -rl secondary_doc api/test/ exits 1 with no output: zero coverage for either half of D175. bp search for a built bucket-precondition gate returned 492 hits and none is one. GitHub branch protection returns 404 'Branch not protected' and rulesets are empty — no check is a mechanical merge block; enforcement is doctrine-level.

PARTIAL: components.ex was read only through measure.mjs's citations by the round-trip verifier. The compound D175 cell was NOT reached by the instrument and cannot be — it drills root, Papers, paper and never opens a secondary pane, confirmed structurally. No observed probe row has ever come from inside runRoundTrip's loop; the bucket guarantee there rests on code reading (descending WIDTHS, a preceding page.goto, and 1440 clearing every +32 edge), which is itself an argument for shipping the assertion rather than ruling it.
Decisions — D182 to D189, each with its one-line why

D182 — Round-trip fidelity HOLDS; D161(i) is PAID by measurement. WHY: 27/27 bit-identical across three independent runs on one deployed sha, with zero cell diffs between runs — the epic's oldest open thread, closed in the affirmative.

D183 — The dismiss_control scalar is a half-truth and may never be quoted; D161(ii) is MET. WHY: the scalar reads widths[0] alone and hides that every destination width has a purpose-built dismiss affordance, understating the condition it reports on.

D184 — The exit code cannot gate the round trip. WHY: a failed open leg abandons all 27 cells and still exits 0, so gates must read round_trip.ran and returns_bit_identical, and the COMMITTED artefact must be one where ran is true.

D185 — D171's precondition is absent from code; ship it in the RAW band form, report never die. WHY: a held-bucket-aware mirror agrees BY CONSTRUCTION including in the exact case D171 exists to catch — a tautology wearing a guard's uniform — while the structural guarantee is real but WIDTHS[0]-dependent with nothing guarding the dependency.

D186 — The 1024 position:static warnings are a stale expectation, neither drift nor flake. WHY: zero variance across four runs plus a traced cause (the ladder, proven inside the compared range) makes them the ladder's CONFIRMING rows; the assertion must NARROW to standard AND panel <= 860, not be silenced, or the epic loses a live tripwire.

D187 — D175's compound state is reachable and PAINTS; D96 is refuted. WHY: executed through real affordances with pixel evidence, on a cell the instrument structurally cannot reach — so the bracket must declare it out-of-matrix in words, or the artefact reads as 'no scrim renders anywhere', which is demonstrably false.

D188 — The terminal run fires WITHOUT --positive-control; zero_cause may not read DESK-FIXED (proven). WHY: the shipped flag is an executed false green that wins with or without the generator, so quoting it would certify a guard that isn't sound.

D189 — The prediction is a committed frozen file, split from its checker. WHY: prose registration cannot be mechanically checked, and freezing data with logic forces a choice between shipping a known-buggy checker and breaking the freeze — the prototype had a real bug within minutes.

D127(a) — round-trip fidelity, unmeasured since D127 was written — returns the reading column bit-identical at 27 of 27 cells on the deployed build, re-confirmed by Review in three further full runs against bc64d869a3a82beb1b39824196f60236b2082dbc / slot blue, bracketed PRE and POST. What shipped, per slice

B — spd-w13-instrument-bucket-precondition. Final branch loop-epic/the-instrument-asserts-its-own-bucket-pr-1-r (CARRIES THE CHARTER). Gate re-run green on Review's final state: 54 rows, bracket matched, 3 warnings (all pre-existing in-floor-ch, already filed at wave 8), bucket_precondition checked 54 / agreed 54. D171/D185's precondition now checks 72 readings per full run where the count was previously 0, in the RAW bandNameFor form; D183's dismiss half-truth replaced by a per-width table plus rollup; D186's overlayAsserted narrowed to standard AND panel <= 860 rather than silenced. VERDICT: excellent, and the single strongest slice of the wave.

C — spd-w13-prediction-registered. Final branch loop-epic/register-the-terminal-run-s-prediction-a-2-r. Gate green (UNEVALUATED, exit 3, against the round-trip-less committed artefact — the correct answer). The repo's first committed prediction file, frozen, split from a fixable checker that recomputes every verdict and never trusts a row's own. VERDICT: the format is sound and genuinely falsifiable; Review fixed one cross-slice defect in it (below).

D — spd-w13-d175-compound-repro. Final branch loop-epic/commit-the-d175-compound-state-repro-the-3-r. Gate re-run LIVE by Review: 9/9 PASS on bc64d869a, .editor-panel 620px exact, scrim painting confirmed by computed style with the pixel pair as its photograph; --simulate-fixed-build re-proven to go RED on exactly the three scrim-dependent checks while geometry and bracket stay PASS. VERDICT: honest about its own limits to an exemplary degree.

A — scrim-threshold-forced-container-control. NOT rebuilt, and correctly so: the rescue had already been performed by its claim holder while this wave was dispatching. PR #5098 is open, rebases clean, and its gate passes. It needs a MERGE DECISION, not a builder.
What Review fixed in place — two of them defects no single builder could have seen

1. THE BUCKET PRECONDITION DID NOT REACH THE ROUND-TRIP CELLS (slice B). A width whose stamp disagreed with the raw band warned and was flagged, but its three face cells still counted toward cells/identical_cells — so returns_bit_identical, the headline this wave exists to establish and the exact value round 2's gate asserts, could be computed partly over a comparison of two DIFFERENT TIERS. The builder found this and filed it rather than fixing it, reasoning it changed the headline metric and was not briefed. It sits on the wish's own metric, so Review closed it. Withdrawn cells now report identical:null (never false), carry their recomputable answer, are counted visibly, and full coverage is required before the claim is made. PROVEN BY MUTATION: band edge 640 -> 700 gives 64/72 preconditions, 3 cells withdrawn at 640, and returns_bit_identical FALSE on a 24-of-24-identical sweep that would previously have read 27/27 TRUE.

2. A GENUINE CROSS-SLICE DEFECT (slice C). C's dismiss-grammar check read the run-level rt.dismiss_control scalar and skipped itself when that scalar was absent — and B DELETES that scalar, by D183, by name. Merged as-is, two individually-correct slices would have produced a guard that CANNOT FAIL on the exact affordance condition D161(ii) turns on, silently and green: the epic's oldest recurring disease, introduced by the act of merging. The checker now reads the per-width table D183 makes citable, treats a missing grammar as a MISS rather than a silent skip, and still honours the retired scalar so pre- and post-D183 artefacts both read. The frozen prediction was NOT touched — precisely the split D189 exists to permit. Proven by four mutations, including an unruled control on both the new and legacy paths.

3. A COLD-READER GAP (slice D). L4's failure could not distinguish 'the desk removed the picker' from 'today's unpinned first task happens to lack one' — two very different findings printing identically, in a file whose whole purpose is cold-reader re-runnability. It now names the opened task, says whether it was pinned, and tells an unpinned reader to re-run with --task before filing a desk regression.
The finding this wave produced by accident, and it governs round 2

Running C's checker against a REAL round-trip artefact — which no builder ever had, and which only existed because B's slice produced one — gives exit 1 with 24 misses, ALL at viewport 1280, all three faces, alongside 0 self-inconsistencies and 27/27 cells returned unchanged. content_px at 1280 reads 640 where the 2026-07-20 table (sha 65541e2d) recorded 596: exactly +44px, the collapsed-strip width, deterministic across three independent runs. This is NOT a round-trip failure — before and after moved together. It is the desk having genuinely moved at one width, caught by a prior-observation basis doing exactly the job D189 designed it for. THE PREDICTION STAYS FROZEN: one edited to match the run it governs is worthless. ROUND 2 MUST THEREFORE NOT GATE GREEN ON check-prediction EXITING 0 — gate on round_trip.ran && returns_bit_identical (D184) and REPORT the 1280 misses as registered staleness. Filed as spd-w13-1280-prior-observations-stale (p1, published).
Ledger audit

HONEST — no lies to fix. All four wave tasks read lifecycle in_progress with a top-level claim.worker (B epoch 8, C epoch 6, D epoch 7, A epoch 7 under lead-truthgrip), parented to the epic root, wave_paper linked, every non-merge criterion stamped with substantial evidence (363–1224 bytes) as the builders worked, and the merge-gated final criterion correctly met:false with empty evidence for the lead. The epic root sits open at 0/12, correct for a round-2 slice. Review briefly mis-read content.claim (null) instead of the top-level claim and nearly 'fixed' a non-problem; the correction is recorded here because the near-miss is the lesson. Leases were pulsed with attributed review now-lines so none lapses before merge — a lapse is what breaks pr-task-gate. Builder-filed residue verified published: spd-w13-roundtrip-precondition-does-not-withdraw-cells (now FIXED by Review, both criteria stamped with mutation evidence, left in_progress as merge-gated) and spd-check-prediction-fixtures-committed (left open — committing 700KB-derived fixtures is a real design call, not a review edit). No task outside this wave was touched.
Grade — A−

EARNED, not given. Three slices, three genuinely hard proofs, and an unusual degree of builder honesty: every one of them volunteered the weakness that mattered most, and in slice B's case filed the exact hole Review then closed. The wish is answered in the affirmative with the strongest evidence this epic has produced — a bit-identical round trip on the deployed build, now guarded by a precondition that is mutation-proven to fire and by a coverage rule that refuses to make the claim on a partial sweep. Bloat is low; every file added earns its place; the D175 repro is a model of stating its own limits.

DOCKED for three things. (1) The cross-slice dismiss-grammar defect was latent in the wave as built — two correct slices that jointly create a vacuous guard is exactly the failure mode the charter keeps re-litigating, and it reached Review rather than Decide's file-fence. (2) The round-trip cell-withdrawal hole was correctly identified by its own builder and then left, on the wave's headline metric; filing is better than hiding, but this one was inside the slice's remit. (3) The wave-13 charter (D182–D189) was stranded on LOCAL MAIN for the SEVENTH recorded time, and Review again had to rescue it onto a merging branch — a defect the charter itself has now documented six times without the process changing. Not docked for round 2's absence: that is the sequenced-rounds law working as designed.
What the lead must know before merging

1. B's -r branch CARRIES THE CHARTER (D182–D189 plus the wave-13 review log). If B is dropped, every decision C and D cite resolves to nothing on origin/main — the 7th recurrence, unrescued. 2. Merge B BEFORE C: they are file-disjoint and will not conflict, but C's fix is what stops B's scalar deletion from silently voiding a guard, and B-then-C is the order the evidence was gathered in. 3. A (#5098) needs a merge decision; its remaining reds (Format, Vercel) are content-impossible for a two-.mjs diff. 4. CLOSE THE MERGE-GATED CRITERION on each task: B index 8, C index 9, D index 8, A index 8 — plus both criteria on spd-w13-roundtrip-precondition-does-not-withdraw-cells, which Review stamped but left in_progress. 5. Round 2 is inspector-shape-bracketed-deployed-run, dispatched after A+B+C merge AND guerrilla serves the merge SHA (D47/D63) — and it must gate per the 1280 finding above.

A width whose stamp disagreed with the raw band warned and was flagged, but its three face cells still counted toward cells/identical_cells — so returns_bit_identical, the headline this wave exists to establish and the exact value round 2's gate asserts, could be computed partly over a comparison of two DIFFERENT TIERS. The builder found this and filed it rather than fixing it, reasoning it changed the headline metric and was not briefed. It sits on the wish's own metric, so Review closed it. Withdrawn cells now report identical:null (never false), carry their recomputable answer, are counted visibly, and full coverage is required before the claim is made. PROVEN BY MUTATION: band edge 640 -> 700 gives 64/72 preconditions, 3 cells withdrawn at 640, and returns_bit_identical FALSE on a 24-of-24-identical sweep that would previously have read 27/27 TRUE.

2. A GENUINE CROSS-SLICE DEFECT (slice C). C's dismiss-grammar check read the run-level rt.dismiss_control scalar and skipped itself when that scalar was absent — and B DELETES that scalar, by D183, by name. Merged as-is, two individually-correct slices would have produced a guard that CANNOT FAIL on the exact affordance condition D161(ii) turns on, silently and green: the epic's oldest recurring disease, introduced by the act of merging. The checker now reads the per-width table D183 makes citable, treats a missing grammar as a MISS rather than a silent skip, and still honours the retired scalar so pre- and post-D183 artefacts both read. The frozen prediction was NOT touched — precisely the split D189 exists to permit. Proven by four mutations, including an unruled control on both the new and legacy paths.

3. A COLD-READER GAP (slice D). L4's failure could not distinguish 'the desk removed the picker' from 'today's unpinned first task happens to lack one' — two very different findings printing identically, in a file whose whole purpose is cold-reader re-runnability. It now names the opened task, says whether it was pinned, and tells an unpinned reader to re-run with --task before filing a desk regression.

The finding this wave produced by accident, and it governs round 2

Running C's checker against a REAL round-trip artefact — which no builder ever had, and which only existed because B's slice produced one — gives exit 1 with 24 misses, ALL at viewport 1280, all three faces, alongside 0 self-inconsistencies and 27/27 cells returned unchanged. content_px at 1280 reads 640 where the 2026-07-20 table (sha 65541e2d) recorded 596: exactly +44px, the collapsed-strip width, deterministic across three independent runs. This is NOT a round-trip failure — before and after moved together. It is the desk having genuinely moved at one width, caught by a prior-observation basis doing exactly the job D189 designed it for. THE PREDICTION STAYS FROZEN: one edited to match the run it governs is worthless. ROUND 2 MUST THEREFORE NOT GATE GREEN ON check-prediction EXITING 0 — gate on round_trip.ran && returns_bit_identical (D184) and REPORT the 1280 misses as registered staleness. Filed as spd-w13-1280-prior-observations-stale (p1, published).

Ledger audit

HONEST — no lies to fix. All four wave tasks read lifecycle in_progress with a top-level claim.worker (B epoch 8, C epoch 6, D epoch 7, A epoch 7 under lead-truthgrip), parented to the epic root, wave_paper linked, every non-merge criterion stamped with substantial evidence (363–1224 bytes) as the builders worked, and the merge-gated final criterion correctly met:false with empty evidence for the lead. The epic root sits open at 0/12, correct for a round-2 slice. Review briefly mis-read content.claim (null) instead of the top-level claim and nearly 'fixed' a non-problem; the correction is recorded here because the near-miss is the lesson. Leases were pulsed with attributed review now-lines so none lapses before merge — a lapse is what breaks pr-task-gate. Builder-filed residue verified published: spd-w13-roundtrip-precondition-does-not-withdraw-cells (now FIXED by Review, both criteria stamped with mutation evidence, left in_progress as merge-gated) and spd-check-prediction-fixtures-committed (left open — committing 700KB-derived fixtures is a real design call, not a review edit). No task outside this wave was touched.

Grade — A−

EARNED, not given. Three slices, three genuinely hard proofs, and an unusual degree of builder honesty: every one of them volunteered the weakness that mattered most, and in slice B's case filed the exact hole Review then closed. The wish is answered in the affirmative with the strongest evidence this epic has produced — a bit-identical round trip on the deployed build, now guarded by a precondition that is mutation-proven to fire and by a coverage rule that refuses to make the claim on a partial sweep. Bloat is low; every file added earns its place; the D175 repro is a model of stating its own limits.

DOCKED for three things. (1) The cross-slice dismiss-grammar defect was latent in the wave as built — two correct slices that jointly create a vacuous guard is exactly the failure mode the charter keeps re-litigating, and it reached Review rather than Decide's file-fence. (2) The round-trip cell-withdrawal hole was correctly identified by its own builder and then left, on the wave's headline metric; filing is better than hiding, but this one was inside the slice's remit. (3) The wave-13 charter (D182–D189) was stranded on LOCAL MAIN for the SEVENTH recorded time, and Review again had to rescue it onto a merging branch — a defect the charter itself has now documented six times without the process changing. Not docked for round 2's absence: that is the sequenced-rounds law working as designed.

What the lead must know before merging

1. B's -r branch CARRIES THE CHARTER (D182–D189 plus the wave-13 review log). If B is dropped, every decision C and D cite resolves to nothing on origin/main — the 7th recurrence, unrescued. 2. Merge B BEFORE C: they are file-disjoint and will not conflict, but C's fix is what stops B's scalar deletion from silently voiding a guard, and B-then-C is the order the evidence was gathered in. 3. A (#5098) needs a merge decision; its remaining reds (Format, Vercel) are content-impossible for a two-.mjs diff. 4. CLOSE THE MERGE-GATED CRITERION on each task: B index 8, C index 9, D index 8, A index 8 — plus both criteria on spd-w13-roundtrip-precondition-does-not-withdraw-cells, which Review stamped but left in_progress. 5. Round 2 is inspector-shape-bracketed-deployed-run, dispatched after A+B+C merge AND guerrilla serves the merge SHA (D47/D63) — and it must gate per the 1280 finding above.
